We are going to explore our Dixon-Coles model. This notebook should be sufficient
for assessment.

We are going to implement a dixon coles model for goalscored in a game. We will then explore modifications to the model given time. As always, let us star by loading our initial dataset.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)

epl_1718 <- read.csv("https://www.football-data.co.uk/mmz4281/1718/E0.csv")

epl_1718 <- epl_1718 %>%
  select(HomeTeam, AwayTeam, FTHG, FTAG) %>%
  rename(HomeGoals = FTHG, AwayGoals = FTAG)

head(epl_1718)
```
### On the dixon coles model:
The famous model introduced in M.Dixon & S.Coles (1996) is a riff on the poisson model introduced in M.Maher (1982). A notable change is the addition of a corrective function which increases the probability, under the model, of seeing low scoring draws as full time results.

The model is as defined as follows:

$$P(X=x,Y=y)=\tau_{\lambda,\mu}(x,y;\rho)\frac{e^{-\lambda}\lambda^x}{x!}\frac{e^{-\mu}\mu^y}{y!},$$
where $\tau_{\lambda,\mu}(x,y;\rho)$ is the correction term defined by:

$$\tau_{\lambda,\mu}(x,y;\rho)= \begin{cases} 1-\lambda\mu\rho, & (x,y)=(0,0),\\ 1+\lambda\rho, & (x,y)=(0,1),\\ 1+\mu\rho, & (x,y)=(1,0),\\ 1-\rho, & (x,y)=(1,1),\\ 1, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}$$

We implement this below:

```{r}
dixon_coles_game_model <- function(team_ratings, home_team, away_team, 
                                   home_advantage, rho, max_goals = 10) {
  
  ###--- extract the team ratings ---###
  alpha_i <- team_ratings[[home_team]]$attack_rating
  beta_i  <- team_ratings[[home_team]]$def_rating
  alpha_j <- team_ratings[[away_team]]$attack_rating
  beta_j  <- team_ratings[[away_team]]$def_rating
  
  ###--- lambda and mu rates for goals scored by home and away teams ---###
  lambda <- alpha_i * beta_j * (1+ home_advantage)
  mu     <- alpha_j * beta_i
  
  ###--- grid of possible scorelines as upto max allowed by param ---###
  scores <- expand.grid(home_goals= 0:max_goals, away_goals= 0:max_goals)
  
  x <- scores$home_goals
  y <- scores$away_goals
  
  ###--- prob of scoreline under independent poisson ---### 
  prob <- dpois(x, lambda) * dpois(y, mu)
  
  ###--- calc dixon-coles correction ---###
  tau <- rep(1, nrow(scores))
  
  tau[x == 0 & y == 0] <- 1 - lambda * mu * rho
  tau[x == 0 & y == 1] <- 1 + lambda * rho
  tau[x == 1 & y == 0] <- 1 + mu * rho
  tau[x == 1 & y == 1] <- 1 - rho
  
  ###--- apply correction ---###
  prob <- prob * tau
  
  ###--- normalise probabilities over the scorelines ---###
  prob <- prob / sum(prob)
  
  ###--- take sample from the adjusted probs ---###
  i <- sample.int(nrow(scores), size = 1, prob = prob)
  
  return(c(home_goals = scores$home_goals[i], away_goals = scores$away_goals[i]))
}
```

We will assume that home advantage, and rho follow those found in recent studies by [INSERT SOURCE HERE]. Now, we will try to estimate attack and defence ratings for each team after the 2018-2019 premier league.

```{r}

fit_dixon_coles <- function(data,
                            home_advantage = 0.05,
                            rho = -0.05) {

  # Keep only matches with complete scores
  required <- c("HomeTeam", "AwayTeam", "HomeGoals", "AwayGoals")
  data <- data[complete.cases(data[, required]), required]

  if (nrow(data) == 0) {
    stop("No complete matches available for fitting.")
  }

  if (home_advantage <= -1) {
    stop("home_advantage must be greater than -1.")
  }

  # Identify teams and their indices
  teams <- sort(unique(c(data$HomeTeam, data$AwayTeam)))
  n <- length(teams)

  home_idx <- match(data$HomeTeam, teams)
  away_idx <- match(data$AwayTeam, teams)

  x <- data$HomeGoals
  y <- data$AwayGoals

  # Negative log-likelihood
  neg_log_likelihood <- function(par) {

    # First n-1 log-attack ratings are free.
    # The final one enforces sum(log_attack) = 0.
    log_attack <- c(
      par[1:(n - 1)],
      -sum(par[1:(n - 1)])
    )

    # Remaining n parameters are log-defence ratings
    log_def <- par[n:(2 * n - 1)]

    # Expected goals for each observed match
    lambda <- exp(log_attack[home_idx] + log_def[away_idx]) *
      (1 + home_advantage)

    mu <- exp(log_attack[away_idx] + log_def[home_idx])

    # Dixon-Coles correction
    tau <- rep(1, length(x))

    idx00 <- x == 0 & y == 0
    idx01 <- x == 0 & y == 1
    idx10 <- x == 1 & y == 0
    idx11 <- x == 1 & y == 1

    tau[idx00] <- 1 - lambda[idx00] * mu[idx00] * rho
    tau[idx01] <- 1 + lambda[idx01] * rho
    tau[idx10] <- 1 + mu[idx10] * rho
    tau[idx11] <- 1 - rho

    # The correction must produce valid probabilities
    if (any(!is.finite(tau)) || any(tau <= 0)) {
      return(1e100)
    }

    # Log-likelihood of each observed score
    log_likelihood <- dpois(x, lambda, log = TRUE) +
      dpois(y, mu, log = TRUE) +
      log(tau)

    if (any(!is.finite(log_likelihood))) {
      return(1e100)
    }

    # optim() minimises, so return negative log-likelihood
    -sum(log_likelihood)
  }

  # Initial values: all attack and defence ratings equal 1
  initial_par <- rep(0, 2 * n - 1)

  # Estimate the parameters
  fit <- optim(
    par = initial_par,
    fn = neg_log_likelihood,
    method = "BFGS",
    hessian = TRUE,
    control = list(maxit = 10000)
  )

  # Recover the fitted ratings
  log_attack <- c(
    fit$par[1:(n - 1)],
    -sum(fit$par[1:(n - 1)])
  )

  log_def <- fit$par[n:(2 * n - 1)]

  # Return the named list expected by your simulator
  team_ratings <- setNames(
    lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
      list(
        attack_rating = exp(log_attack[i]),
        def_rating = exp(log_def[i])
      )
    }),
    teams
  )

  list(
    team_ratings = team_ratings,
    convergence = fit$convergence,
    negative_log_likelihood = fit$value,
    optimiser = fit
  )
}

```
Now let us fit our data.
```{r}
fit <- fit_dixon_coles(
  data = epl_1718,
  home_advantage = 0.05,
  rho = -0.05
)

team_ratings <- fit$team_ratings

# Inspect the fitted ratings for Arsenal
team_ratings$Arsenal

# Check optimisation status
fit$convergence

# Compare model fits using this value
fit$negative_log_likelihood
```
Let us source our season 
```{r}
predicted_league_table = SSIG(team_ratings= team_ratings, game_model= dc_game_model)
print(predicted_league_table)
```
